correctness.rationale: For arbitrary independently adjustable reversible edge flows, conjugation by sqrt of stationary masses expresses SLEM as an affine symmetric spectral norm, hence convex. The mass-preserving dihedral subgroup is edge-transitive, so averaging proves that a homogeneous edge-flow optimizer exists globally. Exact two-by-two Fourier blocks yield the entire nonstationary spectrum and reduce its SLEM to max(1-alpha*G,abs(1-2*(1+r)*alpha)); the two extreme rates are attained and all intermediate rates cannot exceed them. The scalar piecewise-linear minimax yields alpha=min(1/2,2/(2*(1+r)+G)) and the exact boundary r=1-sin^2(pi/m)/2. Direct exact algebra checks all endpoint regimes, including m=2 and r=1; numerical matrix and unrestricted-conductance computations independently test finite samples only. The analytic steps cover every integer m>=2 and real 0<r<=1.

The novel implication is derived by constructing the two-band spectrum and optimizing its nonstationary extreme modes subject to heterogeneous holding constraints. Existing 2004 SDP theory does provide a computational route for any instance, but no inspected source makes the all-m/r closed-form implication. No claim of new uniform-cycle formula, stationarity-reversibility definition, or symmetry-averaging principle is made.

value.rationale: The precise r<=1-(1/2)sin^2(pi/m) criterion decides, for every size and every alternating mass ratio, when the familiar Metropolis-Hastings proposal is exactly optimal among all reversible same-support kernels. When it is not, the theorem supplies the optimal amount of holding and exact SLEM, with an asymptotic sharp bias threshold. This is a motivated all-parameter Markov-chain design classification, not an arbitrary isolated small-graph computation or a rewording of the known uniform cycle.
